Definition: literally a director, i.e. the spindle or shank of a distaff, by which it is twirled
BiblicalUsage: Kishor is the spindle, the shank of the distaff by which it is twirled. Proverbs 31:19 pictures the virtuous woman at her work: she layeth her hands to the spindle, and her hands hold the distaff.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the spindle is the whole portrait in one verse: her hands are busy, her work is skilled, and her diligence is done at home where no one applauds it.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
